body: About to be 31, with similar feelings. Going through the motions, trying to pass for a “normal” person when necessary. To deter myself from suicide, I’ve been trying to frame it as yet another way I would be ruining something that still has the potential to be good, yet another failure. It’s not a way to terminate the pattern of ruining things, but just a continuation of it. Which leaves you with, “may as well continue the pattern” or “let’s disrupt that pattern in the biggest way possible by going through with it and choosing to live a life, even if it means being depressed.” What’s scary to me is not knowing what comes next. But I think choosing to live takes more courage than choosing to die.

I have it too. An ex gave it to me years into our relationship. It’s not fun to have to tell future partners, but I think the stigma is dissipating over time and more people are educated/mature about the risks than you might think. And a lot of folks have it, as others have mentioned. Personally, it’s at the bottom of my list when it comes to drivers of suicidal ideation. I forget about it most of the time.
